In [[mathematics]], '''Malmquist's theorem''', is the name of any of the three theorems proved by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Axel Johannes Malmquist|first=Axel Johannes |last=Malmquist|year1=1913|year2=1920|year3=1941}}.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Malmquist |first=J. |date=1913 |title=Sur les fonctions a un nombre fini de branches définies par les équations différentielles du premier ordre |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1485887356 |journal=Acta Mathematica |language=en |volume=36 |issue=0 |pages=297–343 |doi=10.1007/BF02422385 |issn=0001-5962|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Malmquist |first=J. |date=1920 |title=Sur les fonctions à un nombre fini de branches satisfaisant à une équation différentielle du premier ordre |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1485887525 |journal=Acta Mathematica |language=en |volume=42 |issue=0 |pages=317–325 |doi=10.1007/BF02404413 |issn=0001-5962}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Malmquist |first=J. |date=1941 |title=Sur les fonctions à un nombre fini de branches satisfaisant à une équation différentielle du premier ordre |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1485888343 |journal=Acta Mathematica |language=en |volume=74 |issue=0 |pages=175–196 |doi=10.1007/BF02392253 |issn=0001-5962}}</ref> These theorems restrict the forms of first order algebraic [[differential equation]]s which have transcendental [[meromorphic]] or algebroid solutions.

==Statement of the theorems==
Theorem (1913). If the differential equation
:<math>\frac{dw}{dz}=R(z,w)</math>
where ''R''(''z'',''w'') is a [[rational function]], has a transcendental [[meromorphic function|meromorphic]] solution, then ''R'' is a [[polynomial]] of degree at most 2 with respect to ''w''; in other words the differential equation is a [[Riccati equation]], or linear.

Theorem (1920). If an irreducible differential equation
:<math>F\left(\frac{dw}{dz},w,z\right)=0</math>
where ''F'' is a polynomial, has a transcendental meromorphic solution, then the equation has no [[movable singularity|movable singularities]]. Moreover, it can be algebraically reduced either to a Riccati equation or to
:<math>\left(\frac{dw}{dz}\right)^2=a(z)P(z,w),</math>
where ''P'' is a polynomial of degree ''3'' with respect to ''w''.

Theorem (1941). If an irreducible differential equation
:<math>F\left(\frac{dw}{dz},w,z\right)=0,</math>
where ''F'' is a polynomial, has a transcendental [[algebroid function|algebroid]] solution, then it can be algebraically reduced to an equation that has no movable singularities.

A modern account of theorems 1913, 1920 is given in the paper of [[Alexandre Eremenko|A. Eremenko]] (1982).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Eremenko |first=A E |date=1982-08-31 |title=Meromorphic solutions of algebraic differential equations |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/rm3769 |journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys |volume=37 |issue=4 |pages=61–95 |doi=10.1070/RM1982v037n04ABEH003967 |issn=0036-0279|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
